_about: Why each term exists and who confirmed it: the delivery lead's questions, confirmed by Chiheb Dkhil on 2026-10-07 (B6); the three states, transitions and blocks of release 2 (roadmap M1-M3), awaiting confirmation.

WorkItem.question: What is planned, by whom, and what is blocked? (WK1-WK3)
WorkItem.why: The unit the delivery lead plans and the one thing that links the plan to what the product specifies and the estate holds.
WorkItem.alternatives: Epic, Story and Task as classes: rejected, one class with a kind answers the same questions and a story that becomes an epic is a changed attribute, not a changed class.
WorkItem.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-07 (B6, the delivery lead's questions)

Milestone.question: What is planned for this milestone? (WK1)
Milestone.why: A release ships; a milestone is reached. Both schedule work, and a demo is not a release.
Milestone.alternatives: Milestone as a kind of Release: rejected, a release is the product's scope boundary and carries what shipped.
Milestone.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-07 (B6, the delivery lead's questions)

Transition.question: Where is this item now, and how did it get there? (WK12, WK13)
Transition.why: A state written on an item is overwritten and its history lost; a state appended as a dated, attributed transition keeps every change, lets a merged pull request or a promotion set it the same way a person does, and answers what the state was on any date through the superseded chain.
Transition.alternatives: A `state` attribute set by hand: rejected, no history and no event can set it. A `history` list on the item: rejected, a fact per change is what supersession already does.

Block.question: What is blocked, since when, why, and on whom? (WK11)
Block.why: A blocked item without a reason and someone to ask is a stuck item nobody can unstick. The block carries both, and the shape refuses one without them.
Block.alternatives: Reason and waiting-on as attributes of the item: rejected, they belong to the blocking, not the item, and vanish when it is unblocked. A Block unrelated to Transition: rejected, blocking is a change of state.

Person.question: Whom does a blocked item wait on, and who raised the block? (WK11)
Person.why: A role or a team says what, not who; a block waits on a person who can answer, and a message goes to a person. The communication pack maps a git identity to one.
Person.alternatives: Role only: rejected, the lead asks a person, and the roadmap's notify command needs one.

delivers.question: Which requirements slip if this component is late? (WK5)
delivers.why: The one edge from the plan to the other levels: an item delivers a requirement, a feature, a component. Without it the plan is a list.
delivers.alternatives: Separate relations per target class: rejected, one question walks them all.
delivers.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-07 (B6, the delivery lead's questions)

blocked_by.question: What blocks this item, and whose call is it? (WK3, WK7)
blocked_by.why: A blocker is a thing in the graph (a risk, an open question, a decision, another item), so the question answers who owns it.
blocked_by.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-07 (B6, the delivery lead's questions)

scheduled_in.question: What is planned for this milestone or release? (WK1, WK4)
scheduled_in.why: The plan is work placed in time: without the milestone or release an item is scheduled in, no question about a date can run.
scheduled_in.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-07 (B6, the delivery lead's questions)

assigned_to.question: What is this team working on? (WK2)
assigned_to.why: Work is done by teams; a role when one function is the point.
assigned_to.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-07 (B6, the delivery lead's questions)

transition_of.question: Where is this item now? (WK13)
transition_of.why: The one edge from a change of state to the item it moves; exactly one, or the change moves nothing or two things.
transition_of.alternatives: An item id attribute on the transition: rejected, an edge is what the engine checks and walks.

waiting_on.question: What is blocked, and on whom? (WK11)
waiting_on.why: Whom to tell is the point of recording a block: a person, a team, an item, a decision, a question or a risk, each a thing in the graph that can be asked or watched.
waiting_on.alternatives: Reuse blocked_by: rejected, blocked_by is a standing dependency the plan records and may hold while the item is open; waiting_on is what this block waits on and goes when the block does.
